newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel watchdog slams Boeing-McDonnell plan.
newsitem.headline: German cartel watchdog slams Boeing-McDonnell plan.

text.p: The president of Germany's Federal Cartel Office on Sunday reaffirmed European opposition to the proposed $14 billion merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas.
"If Europeans don't act now, while they still can, then it is possible that in a few years we will have a world monopoly in aircraft manufacture," Dieter Wolf told the Welt am Sonntag weekly.
Wolf said Europe would use the same principles to block the global merger as the Americans used to stop the effects of European mergers in their country.

The European Commission is set on Wednesday to block the proposed merger between the two U.S. aircraft makers as it believes that the deal would strengthen Boeing's already dominant position in the commercial sector.
EU leaders have backed the commission.

Wolf said that as the largest manufacturer of military aeroplanes, McDonnell Douglas received huge subsidies from the U.S. government. The know-how which Boeing would gain from the merger would put pressure on the competition.
